Blocks.Text: The Organization Content Revisions API returns version history and content revisions for an organization's Life Pages (also known as Targeted Content pages or Career Pages). Life Pages allow companies to create customized page experiences for different audiences (e.g., by location, job function, or seniority level). This API tracks all revisions of Life Page content, including drafts, published versions, and historical changes.
Product Name Translation:

Current: Life Page, Targeted Content
Legacy: Career Pages
Hierarchy: Company Page → Organization → Organizational Page → Life Page
Each content revision represents a snapshot of Life Page configuration, including:

Multiple targeted content variations for different audiences.
Default fallback content when no targeting criteria match.
Publishing status and revision history
Auto-save and migration tracking
To use the Organization Content Revisions API, you need:

Required Role: The authenticated user must have one of these organization page roles:

ADMINISTRATOR
CONTENT_ADMINISTRATOR


How to Find Organizations You Can Query?

Call OrganizationAuthorization's BATCH_FIND by AuthorizationAction and AuthenticatedMember with an authorization action of CareerPageAuthorizationActionType.CAREER_PAGE_LIFE_READ to retrieve eligible organizations.


How to Get Content Revision URNs?
Content Revision URNs are composite identifiers in the format:
 Copy urn:li:organizationContentRevision:(urn:li:organization:{orgId},{revisionId})

Use one of these methods to discover content revision URNs:

History method: Lists all revision history for an organization.
Published method: Returns the currently published revision that's visible to LinkedIn members.
The service currently provides the following methods:

Get - Returns a content revision for a given organization content revision URN.
BatchGet - Batch get content revisions for multiple organization content revision URNs.
History - Retrieve the revision history for an organization (all revisions, including drafts and published).
Published - Retrieve the current published revision for an organization that is served to members.

Rows.Text: Unique targeting attributes paired with the content. Specifying multiple targeted contents with the identical targeting attributes is not allowed.

If none of the targetedContents match, this targeted content should be used as a fallback. Note that it's permitted to re-use a targeted content inside of targetedContents, and if used as a default fallback, the targeting criteria won't be evaluated.
Revision the user started the modification from.

If and when this content revision was published to be viewable by members. Note that while only the newest published content is viewable by members, older content retains the published attribute so administrators are able to inspect which older revisions were published. Also, content revisions that aren't published are considered to be in a draft state, and there is no requirement to ever publish them.
Indicates which saving process (migration, autoSave etc.) this Content Revision was created by.

AuditStamp that records the deletion of this resource, association, or sub-resource. The deleted timestamp must be later than the creation timestamp. Note: It may or may not match the lastModified timestamp, depending on the semantics of the resource, association, or sub-resource.
AuditStamp that records the last modification of this resource, association, or sub-resource. Note: If no modification has happened since creation, lastModified should be the same as created.
When did the resource/association/sub-resource move into the specific lifecycle stage represented by this AuditEvent.

The entity (e.g. a memberUrn, organizationUrn, etc) which will be credited for moving the resource/association/sub-resource into the specific lifecycle stage. It is also the one used to authorize the change.
The entity which performs the change on behalf of the Actor and must be authorized to act as the Actor.

Blocks.Text: Note
Ensure that {ORGANIZATION_URN} and {ORGANIZATION_CONTENT_REVISION_URN} need to be URL-encoded.
An OrganizationContentRevisionUrn is a composite URN constructed using a content revision ID and an organizationUrn.

http


curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaOrganizationContentRevisions/{ORGANIZATION_CONTENT_REVISION_URN}

curl -X GET ''https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaOrganizationContentRevisions/urn%3Ali%3AorganizationContentRevision%3A%28urn%3Ali%3Aorganization%3A1234%2Cd5e2b076-3335-444d-6666-442244ddaa%29'' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {INSERT_TOKEN}' \
--header 'Linkedin-Version: {version number in the format YYYYMM}' \
--header 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0'
An OrganizationContentRevisionUrn is a composite URN constructed using a content revision ID and an organizationUrn.

curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaOrganizationContentRevisions?ids=List(organization_content_revision_id1,organization_content_revision_id2..)

Blocks.Text: Tip

How to determine which organizational pages you can query?
To find the organizations you can query content revisions for, use OrganizationAuthorization's BATCH_FIND by AuthorizationAction and AuthenticatedMember with an authorization action of CareerPageAuthorizationActionType.CAREER_PAGE_LIFE_READ. Returns organizations where you have the necessary permissions to access Life Page content revisions.
An OrganizationContentRevisionUrn is a composite URN constructed using a content revision ID and an organizationUrn.

http


curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaOrganizationContentRevisions?q=history&organization={ORGANIZATION_URN}

curl -X GET ''https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaOrganizationContentRevisions?q=history&organization=urn%3Ali%3Aorganization%3A1234'' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {INSERT_TOKEN}' \
--header 'Linkedin-Version: {version number in the format YYYYMM}' \
--header 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0'

Rows.Text: URN of the organization for which content revisions are requested.
